He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. ==Early life== Pickett grew up in [[Neighborhoods in Washington, D.C.#Ward 6|Ward 6]] of [[Washington, D.C.]]. As a freshman, he attended [[Spingarn High School]] but did not play for the basketball team. After his previous school closed, Pickett moved to [[Eastern High School (Washington, D.C.)|Eastern High School]]. He did not qualify for the team in his sophomore season before playing as a junior and assuming a leading role as a senior. Pickett played a [[postgraduate season]] at [[Massanutten Military Academy]] in [[Woodstock, Virginia]] to gain more interest from college programs.{{cite web |last1=Chen |first1=Nathan |title="I am DC": Jamorko's Journey |url=https://georgetownvoice.com/2021/05/24/i-am-dc-jamorkos-journey/ |website=[[The Georgetown Voice]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=May 24, 2021}} A consensus four-star recruit, he initially committed to playing college basketball for [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] before switching his commitment to [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite news |last1=Wallace |first1=Ava |title=Jamorko Pickett, Ewing's first major recruit to Georgetown, makes a jump as a freshman |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/jamorko-pickett-georgetowns-first-major-recruit-making-a-jump-as-a-freshman/2018/01/26/c764a804-02cc-11e8-8acf-ad2991367d9d_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=January 26, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Cam |title=There's suddenly another 4-star hoops prospect in the Class of 2017 available, and no one has any idea where he's headed |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/theres-suddenly-another-4-star-hoops-prospect-in-the-class-of-2017-available-and-no-one-has-any-idea-where-hes-headed |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=July 17, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Morales |first1=Antonio |title=Ole Miss loses its highest-rated basketball signee Jamarko Pickett |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2017/07/14/ole-miss-loses-its-highest-rated-basketball-signee-jamarko-pickett/480763001/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=July 14, 2017}} ==College career== During his freshman season, Pickett scored a career-high 21 points two times in losses to [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]]. As a freshman, he averaged 9.6 points and 3.7 rebounds per game, and was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite news |last1=Copeland |first1=Kareem |title=Jamorko Pickett and Jahvon Blair have been through just about everything at Georgetown |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/02/26/jamorko-pickett-jahvon-blair-last-standing/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Wolf |first1=Aaron |title=Big Expectations for Jamorko Pickett in his Sophomore Season |url=https://georgetownvoice.com/2018/11/06/big-expectations-for-jamorko-pickett-in-his-sophomore-season/ |website=[[The Georgetown Voice]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=November 6, 2018}} Pickett averaged 6.2 points and 3.8 rebounds per game in his sophomore season. As a junior, he averaged 10.2 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Curran |first1=Aidan |title=Can Georgetown Depend on Jamorko Pickett and Jahvon Blair? |url=https://247sports.com/college/georgetown/Article/Can-Georgetown-Depend-on-Jamorko-Pickett-and-Jahvon-Blair-145291997/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=March 22, 2020}} On December 8, 2020, Pickett recorded 19 points and a career-high 18 rebounds in an 80–48 win against [[Coppin State Eagles men's basketball|Coppin State]].{{cite web |title=Pickett's Double-Double Leads Hoyas to 80-48 Win Over Coppin State |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2020/12/8/mens-basketball-hoyas-return-to-winning-ways-against-coppin-state.aspx |website=Georgetown University Athletics |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=December 8, 2020}} He helped Georgetown win its first [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] title since 2007. As a senior, Pickett averaged 12.2 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Bancroft |first1=Bobby |title=Jamorko Pickett on Wizards Workout, Hoyas & Ewing |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/7/7/22567198/jamorko-pickett-on-wizards-workout-hoyas-ewing |website=Casual Hoya |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=July 7, 2021}} He chose to forgo his additional year of college eligibility and declare for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Movin' On: Georgetown's Jamorko Pickett Going Pro, Hiring an Agent |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2021/5/14/22435879/movin-on-georgetown-hoyas-jamorko-pickett-going-pro-hiring-agent-big-east-jahvon-blair-patrick-ewing |website=Casual Hoya |access-date=August 4, 2021 |date=May 14, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Pickett joined the [[Detroit Pistons]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]],{{cite news|last1=Beard|first1=Rod|title=Young Pistons aim to build 'winning mentality' in Summer League|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2021/08/05/detroit-pistons-release-summer-league-roster/5504558001/|work=[[The Detroit News]]|date=August 5, 2021|access-date=August 9, 2021}} averaging 9.8 points and 3.8 rebounds in five games. On September 24, 2021, Pickett signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pistons, splitting time with the [[Motor City Cruise]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite tweet|number=1441466969782423552|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the club has signed forward Jamorko Pickett to a two-way contract.|user=Pistons_PR|date=September 24, 2021|access-date=September 25, 2021}}{{cite news|last1=Williams|first1=Lauren|title=Detroit Pistons sign Jamorko Pickett to two-way deal|url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/2021/09/detroit-pistons-sign-jamorko-pickett-to-two-way-deal.html|work=[[MLive.com]]|date=September 24, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}} On June 28, 2022, the Pistons decided not to renew Pickett's contract.{{cite tweet|user=JLEdwardsIII|number = 1541896301960380422 | title = Sources: The Pistons will not pick up the team options of Frank Jackson, Luka Garza and Carsen Edwards. Additionally, Detroit's two two-way guys are Braxton Key and Buddy Boeheim, so Jamorko Pickett no longer holds one of those spots.}} ===Cleveland Charge (2022–2023)=== Pickett participated in the
